items.detail: The **S&P 500** gained **1.2%** on the week and the Nasdaq 2.1%, both ending higher even after losing Tuesday's Nasdaq record in a midweek slide.
items.why: Oil kept falling and the AI chip trade came back, which outweighed a bond selloff that knocked tech lower for a day.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield** climbed from below 5% on Monday to **5.20%** on Thursday, its highest since 2007, before holding steady on Friday.
items.why: Flash PMIs showed the fastest US private-sector growth in five years, pushing October Fed hike odds to about 75%.

items.detail: AI megacaps led the week: **AMD topped $1 trillion** in market value on Monday, and Microsoft and Meta powered Friday's gains.
items.why: New AI products from Microsoft and Meta, plus signs that AI spending is still growing, drew buyers back.

items.detail: MSCI's emerging-market index jumped **1.1%** on Monday on hopes for US-China talks, but the gains faded as **Hong Kong's Hang Seng** fell three straight sessions.
items.why: The Trump-Xi summit brought no tariff cuts, and record-high US yields drained appetite for risk.

items.detail: The **Nifty 50** fell **0.9%** to 23,140, its seventh straight weekly loss and the longest losing run since May 2020.
items.why: Foreign investors sold ₹11,490 crore over the week as US yields rose and Brent crude stayed above $100.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** ended the week lower at **2,844**, the only major US index to fall while the Nasdaq gained 2.1%.
items.why: Small caps carry more floating-rate debt, so the jump in yields raised their borrowing costs the most.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** hit an eight-month high near **$86,600** on Tuesday, then slipped back below $84,000 by Saturday.
items.why: Short liquidations drove the early surge, then record-high yields pulled money out of assets that pay no yield.

items.detail: **Ether** peaked near **$2,776** on Tuesday, fell for three days, and steadied around $2,691 by the weekend.
items.why: Rising bets on a Fed hike hit risky coins, even as ETF buying returned with $270 million on Tuesday.

items.detail: **Solana** was the strongest of the three, ending near **$119**, back at the top of its month-long range.
items.why: Spot Solana ETFs extended a 12-week inflow streak, now over $1.16 billion in total, led by Bitwise's BSOL.

items.detail: **Spot gold** fell about **2%** on the week to around $4,293, losing four straight sessions before a small bounce on Friday.
items.why: A dollar near a two-month high and the highest Treasury yields since 2007 made holding bullion more costly.

crossCuttingTheme: Hot US data pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.20%, its highest since 2007, which strengthened the dollar and hurt gold, small caps, Indian stocks and crypto, while cheaper oil kept AI megacaps rising.
